html:
SMTO-LLM-0069 — Runtime not found

GUID: e3b8d336-b434-5237-945a-acb2647bbf28
Slug: local-ai-runtime-not-found
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • SMTO looked for that model server on the Gateway computer, but the Gateway has no record of it. SMTO won't guess and act on a different server that only looks similar.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In a new message, ask SMTO to list the local AI model servers (runtimes) on the Gateway you meant, and choose the one you want from that list. SMTO only acts on a model server using the exact name it recorded, so a typed or old name won't match.
  2. Check that you picked the same Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses on that computer) where the model server was started. Each Gateway keeps its own list, so a model server started on one computer isn't found on another.
  3. If you started the model server from a different workspace in SMTO, switch back to that workspace and ask again. SMTO only shows model servers to the workspace that started them.

What success looks like

  • SMTO lists the model server you meant and can show its details.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer. Don't ask anyone to stop a process just because it uses the same port; it may not be the model server you meant.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The requested Local AI runtime ID is not in this Gateway's runtime records for the current workspace.

What this means

  • The requested runtime ID is absent from this Gateway's retained runtime map. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • The requested runtime ID is absent from this Gateway's retained runtime map.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the runtime ID and Gateway with the current runtime inventory and original start receipt.

How to fix it

  • List runtimes on the profile's Gateway (local_ai.runtimes) and use an exact runtime_id from that list; the record lives in the Gateway's local_ai runtimes.json under its artifact root and is only visible from the workspace that created it. If a record is genuinely missing, investigate it on that Gateway instead of adopting or stopping a process by PID or port.
  • Select the exact retained runtime on its owning Gateway; investigate a missing record without adopting an arbitrary PID.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected runtime ID is present on the Gateway that owns its record.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
